//: The edge fleet. Single source of truth for what exists and where.
//_adding: Adding a location is a new entry here plus `fleet.sh provision <code>`. Nothing in the app or the control plane changes.
//_subnets: Every location needs its own tunnel subnet. Keep allocating /16s out of 10.0.0.0/8 — there is room for 256 of them.
//_priority: Lower wins in auto-selection, and priority is compared BEFORE the client's country. That ordering is what stops every Nigerian user landing on the metered Lagos box; see docs/locations.md.
//_capacity: capacity_peers is a BANDWIDTH budget, not a RAM one. Roughly (monthly transfer) / 40GB per light user. On metered boxes, exceeding it means overage charges, not slowness.

locations.note: Default for auto-selection. Nigeria's submarine cables (MainOne, Glo-1, WACS, Equiano) land in Portugal and the UK, so London is the lowest-latency well-connected hop from Lagos — ahead of Frankfurt.
The bulk-capacity workhorse. Cheapest bandwidth in the fleet by a wide margin, so it absorbs overflow when London fills.
US streaming and services. East coast, not west: ~70ms closer to Lagos via London.
Large Nigerian diaspora and immigration-portal access.
